package_info.package_name: airbnb-env (and related: airbn-geetest3, airbnb-erf, airbnb-i18n-polyglot, airbnb-l10n, airbnb-mediator, airbnb-moment-more-format)
package_info.package_versions: all (only one version per package, e.g., 35.0.0 for Zettle packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are considered malicious because they exploit the dependency confusion attack vector to target internal developer environments of organizations like Airbnb and PayPal Zettle. Upon installation, they collect sensitive system information (username, home directory, hostname, IP address) and transmit it to an external server controlled by the package author. This behavior is not expected from legitimate packages and constitutes an information disclosure risk, even if the intent is proof-of-concept research.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Collects local system information (username, home directory, hostname, IP address) and sends it via HTTPS POST to an external server controlled by the package author.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive system information and exfiltrates it to an external server without user consent or legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not collect and transmit system-level information during installation. Legitimate postinstall scripts are typically used for build steps, not data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or analytics packages may collect anonymized usage data, but this is always disclosed and opt-in.
key_indicators: Use of os module to collect user and system info
Network request to external, non-standard domain during install
No user notification or consent for data collection

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed via dependency confusion (internal package name published to public npm).
Postinstall script executes and collects system information (username, home directory, hostname, IP address).
Collected data is sent via HTTPS POST to attacker's server.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts making network requests
Collection of os.userInfo(), os.homedir(), os.hostname(), or networkInterfaces() during install
Exfiltration of system information to non-standard domains
file_indicators: Presence of code referencing os and https modules together in install scripts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the package's legitimate vendor
Unusual traffic to attacker-controlled endpoints (e.g., attacker.example.com/collect)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access system information and make outbound network requests. Flag packages that collect user, home directory, hostname, or IP address and transmit this data externally. Review package.json for unexpected postinstall hooks and scan for use of os and https modules together. Network monitoring can detect suspicious POST requests to unknown domains during package installation.
